question.problem:
The change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $C$ and the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $C$ are given below. What is $[x]_{B}?$ 

$$
{P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 4 & 3\end{aligned}],\,[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 6\end{aligned}]
$$
question.worked_solution:
We will use the change-of-coordinates formula in the form

$$
[\,x\,]_{B}={P}_{C\to B}[\,x\,]_{C}.
$$

First, we need to find the change-of-coordinates matrix ${P}_{C\to B}$ from $C$ to $B.$ To do that, we compute the inverse of ${P}_{B\to C}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{C\to B} & ={P}_{B\to C}^{-1} \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 4 & 3\end{aligned}]}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{3\cdot 3-4\cdot 2}[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ -4 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ -4 & 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute $[\,x\,]_{B}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{B} & ={P}_{C\to B}[\,x\,]_{C} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ -4 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}7 \\ 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}9 \\ -10\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
